Olga — short answer: doable, but there are compliance details.

Notes: 1) VAT: if the invoice is issued to the EU holding, we need to confirm their VAT registration and whether they will self-account (reverse-charge). If they are VAT-registered in the EU and provide a valid VAT ID, we should issue a net invoice and include a reverse-charge note — no VAT charged by Redwood. If they are not registered, we may need to charge VAT based on place of supply rules.

2) VAT on US subsidiaries: US entities are typically VAT/ sales-tax nil — but local US sales tax rules vary; for software-as-a-service generally no VAT but state-level considerations may apply. We should ask Cumulus for VAT IDs + country of tax registration for each entity.

3) Invoicing format: we can produce a consolidated invoice to the holding company and a separate EOR-style allocation CSV that lists invoice_line_id, amount, currency, cost_center_code, entity_tax_id. The CSV is generated from our billing backend; Marissa can confirm export columns and any associated setup time.

4) Payment instructions: we can include multiple remittance instructions on the parent invoice and in the CSV. If the customer requires separate physical invoices per subsidiary (for bank reconciliation), that adds operational effort and may take 2–3 business days per initial setup.

Happy to join a short call with Cumulus finance.

—Marcus
Director, Revenue Operations
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

- For the pilot: include onboarding fee and first month pro rata lines. We'll map onboarding fee 60% to Cumulus Labs (cost center CL-001) and 40% to Cumulus Therapeutics (CT-002) as a one-off mapping per Ana's worksheet.

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm with Ana the desired one-off allocation percentages for onboarding; 2) customer provides VAT/EIN docs; 3) we enable CSV export and include remittance fields. I attached a sample CSV and a minimal spec doc.
